questions.question: Two adjacent angles that lie on a straight line and sum to 180° form a ____.

solution_key.part2_method: Apply exact mathematical formula or logical deduction step
solution_key.part3_conclusion: By definition, adjacent angles on a straight line form a linear pair and are supplementary.

questions.question: Two intersecting lines form angle x and angle y as a linear pair. If x = 2y, calculate the measures of x and y.
questions.hint_modal: Recall core principles from Chapter 5: Linear pair sum: x + y = 180°. Substitute x = 2y: 2y + y = 1...

solution_key.part2_method: Apply exact mathematical formula or logical deduction step
solution_key.part3_conclusion: Linear pair sum: x + y = 180°. Substitute x = 2y: 2y + y = 180° => 3y = 180° => y = 60°. Then x = 2(60°) = 120°.

questions.question: If two lines intersect and one angle measures 35°, prove the measures of all remaining three angles with geometric reasons.
questions.hint_modal: Recall core principles from Chapter 5: Let angle a = 35°. 1. Angle b forms a linear pair with a: b ...

solution_key.part2_method: Apply exact mathematical formula or logical deduction step
solution_key.part3_conclusion: Let angle a = 35°. 1. Angle b forms a linear pair with a: b = 180° - 35° = 145° (Linear Pair Postulate). 2. Angle c is vertically opposite to a: c = a = 35° (Vertically Opposite Angle Theorem). 3. Angle d is vertically opposite to b: d = b = 145° (Vertically Opposite Angle Theorem). Thus, the four angles are 35°, 145°, 35°, and 145°.

hotspots.title: Intersecting Lines & Angles
hotspots.popover_content: Vertically opposite angles are equal (∠a = ∠c). Linear pairs sum to 180° (∠a + ∠b = 180°).

hotspots.title: Parallel Lines (l || m)
hotspots.popover_content: Coplanar lines that never meet. Maintain constant perpendicular distance throughout.

hotspots.title: Perpendicular Lines (l ⊥ m)
hotspots.popover_content: Lines that intersect at right angles (90°), forming 4 orthogonal quadrants.

hotspots.title: Paper Folding Creases
hotspots.popover_content: Successive horizontal folds yield parallel line creases; orthogonal fold creates perpendicular crease.
